title: Resume Format Checker for Students: Common Layout Traps and How to Fix Them
description: Ensure your student resume passes ATS parsers without layout corruption: margins, fonts, section order, and single-column standards.

image.alt: Resume Formatting Layout Rules for ATS Compliance

body:
The most common reason qualified students get rejected from entry-level tech jobs isn't lack of coding skills — it's document layout corruption. When an applicant tracking system parses a two-column or graphic-heavy resume, the text gets scrambled, causing automated filters to discard the application.

## 1. The 5 Deadliest Layout Mistakes

- Mistake 1: Multi-Column Canva / Word Templates. Parsers read left-to-right across columns, merging disparate text into unintelligible strings.
- Mistake 2: Text in Graphics and Icons. Rating skill levels with star icons (e.g., 'Python ★★★★☆') results in zero extracted skills in the ATS database.
- Mistake 3: Putting Contact Info in Headers/Footers. Many ATS engines strip header and footer zones entirely, omitting your email and phone number.
- Mistake 4: Non-Standard Fonts. Custom decorative fonts may not embed properly in PDFs, leading to corrupted characters.
- Mistake 5: Exceeding 1 Page. For college students, a second page is almost never reviewed by technical screeners.

faq.q: What is the best resume format: PDF or Word?
faq.a: A cleanly generated PDF (from LaTeX or clean Word) is best for modern ATS platforms like Greenhouse and Lever, while standard DOCX is safest for older enterprise portals.
